lines: 1 package is imported by their root in src, so the whole barrel is reachable and the bundler keeps whatever it cannot prove unused:

@nextcloud/vue: 1,172,528 B in 33 modules, 34.6 % of the static path of assistant-assistantPage.mjs, imported by its root in components/TaskListItem.vue (useFormatRelativeTime). It is imported per module as well, through 33 other specifiers.
Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.

5 components of @nextcloud/vue are delivered although no file in src names them, no other dependency names them and no component named by either imports them: 20,583 B, 0.6 % of the static path of assistant-assistantPage.mjs, next to 8 components the source names and 4 those pull in.
NcActionInput 10,230 B, NcPasswordField 4,459 B, NcDateTimePickerNative 4,152 B, NcDateTimePicker 1,162 B, NcColorPicker 580 B.
These arrive through the root import: under a barrel the whole component set is reachable, so the bundler must keep it. Per-component imports leave it free to drop what the app never names.

Known toolchain defect: vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js 3.5.2 in package-lock.json, where the CSS is injected by JavaScript, puts the code that injects the CSS in front of the chunk without shifting its source map, so the map the bundler combines from it loses sources. Here the map of assistant-adminSettings.mjs names 0 of the 1 package its .license file names, and 10 further chunks show the same.
The app runs as built; only the map is short, so the frameworks and libraries are read from the .license files instead.
Fixed in vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js 5.0.0: https://github.com/marco-prontera/vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js/issues/155
Built in a copy with @nextcloud/vite-config 3.0.0-beta.1, the copy does not build: npm install failed with "npm error code ERESOLVE".
